=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1867-2225 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: When a fix-up closes without merging, `wait_ended_at` is set to `${now}` (the current run time, line 2088) instead of the fix-up's closure time, because the fix-up lookup at line 1867 (`--jq '{state, state_reason, labels: [.labels[]?.name]}'`) does not get `closed_at`. The strict `block.at > wait_ended_at` comparison at line 2225 (`unblock_nothing_to_implement_close ... "${wait_ended_at:-${wait_updated:-}}"`) therefore rejects every qualifying "nothing to implement" block posted before the next judge run.
  WHY: The issue is not closed as completed and goes to the model verdict instead. This is the #9215 failure mode that #9518 was filed to fix. The earlier code used `${wait_updated:-}` and would have accepted those blocks. The `block_during_timed_out_wait` test (tests/test_unblock_judge.py:5467-5474) only covers the case where the fix-up is still open and the wait timed out. Both reviewers rated this MAJOR.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2218-2231 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: In unblock_main (around lines 2218-2231), the judge can wrongly close an issue as completed while its fix-up wait is still unresolved, because it passes the wait_updated timestamp as block_after even when the fix-up wait state is not done.
  WHY: The jq filter in unblock_nothing_to_implement_close is true whenever a block's time is later than this timestamp (block.at > after), so issues with a pending fix-up wait are closed. That breaks the rule that blocks filed while the fix-up is unresolved stay with the judge. Rated MAJOR.
- tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py:Test execution | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The pre-push test gate reports a failure in tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py.
  WHY: The pre-push test gate in the PR description says this test failed because of the PR's changes. That points to either a break in the files-touched scope guard or an environment-specific failure, and it has to be resolved for CI to pass. Rated MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_main (around lines 2218-2231) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The judge wrongly closes issues as completed while their fix-up wait is still unresolved.
  WHY: The unblock_main function calls unblock_nothing_to_implement_close with the wait_updated timestamp as the block_after argument even when the fix-up wait state is not done. The jq filter in unblock_nothing_to_implement_close is true when a block occurs after this timestamp (block.at > after), so it closes issues that still have a fix-up wait pending. That breaks the requirement that blocks filed while the fix-up is unresolved must stay with the judge.

  WHY: The pre-push test gate in the PR description says tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py failed because of the PR changes. That suggests either a break in the files-touched scope guard or an environment-specific failure, and it has to be resolved for CI to pass.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:line 1867 (fix-up lookup `--jq '{state, state_reason, labels: [.labels[]?.name]}'`), line 2087-2088 (`wait_ended_at="${now}"`), line 2225 (`unblock_nothing_to_implement_close ... "${wait_ended_at:-${wait_updated:-}}"`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The last run's diff introduced a regression when a fix-up closes without merging. If the fix-up closes before any judge run marks the wait `done`, `wait_ended_at` is set to `${now}` at line 2088, even though the wait really ended at the fix-up's `closed_at`. The lookup at line 1867 does not get `closed_at`, so line 2225 compares every existing block against the current run time and rejects them all. The previous code used `${wait_updated:-}` and accepted blocks posted after the wait comment's last refresh.
  WHY: Take a standalone `ai:blocked` issue whose fix-up closes without the `ai:merged`/`ai:closed` label (for example `state_reason="not_planned"`), after which a "Planning blocked: ... nothing to implement" comment is posted. That issue stays open and is escalated by the model verdict. This is exactly the failure #9518 was filed to fix (#9215's pattern), and it reproduces end to end. The `block_during_timed_out_wait` test (tests/test_unblock_judge.py:5467-5474) only covers the case where the fix-up is still open and the wait timed out, so the existing tests miss the regression.
- TASK_GAP

  Expected change site: scripts/unblock_judge.sh inside `unblock_main`, the no-wait `unblock_nothing_to_implement_close` call site (line 2225)
  Evidence of absence: The PR adds the call site (line 2225), but the comparison at lines 619/2225 fails when the fix-up closed without merging, so the close path does not run in that case and the goal is only partly met.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:Lines 1867, 2082-2088, and 2225 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When a fix-up closes without merging, the judge records the wait end as the current run time, not the fix-up's closure time. The lookup at line 1867 does not include `closed_at`, and line 2088 sets `wait_ended_at` to `${now}`, which line 2225 uses for the strict block timestamp comparison.
  WHY: If the fix-up closes and a qualifying "nothing to implement" block is posted before the next judge run, that block is older than `${now}`. The comparison rejects it, so the judge does not close the issue as completed and goes to the verdict path instead.
